title: How to dictate email without losing control of the message
summary: Learn how to dictate and format email with clear paragraphs, greetings, and sign-offs, then review the message before sending. Includes a Gmail draft example.
body_markdown:
## State the purpose before the wording


Before starting, identify the recipient, the purpose, and any non-negotiable details. For a routine reply, that might be “confirm Thursday’s review, ask for the document by Wednesday, and do not promise a launch date.” You can say the prose yourself or ask for a draft using those constraints.


Treat drafting, checking, and sending as separate decisions.


Use direct dictation when the words are already yours. Use a draft request when you want help composing them, and check the generated text more carefully. A fluent response can introduce an assurance you never intended to make. Neither method removes the need to review a commitment.


VoiceOS’s Dictation Mode enters writing into standard text fields; selected-text editing can revise a passage. Gmail and Outlook integrations expose specific email actions. Review the integration’s scope before assuming the app can manipulate every field in your mail client.\[1\]\[2\]
